newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Grenade attack kills three in eastern Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Grenade attack kills three in eastern Sri Lanka.

text.p: Three people were killed and seven wounded early on Friday in a grenade attack in Sri Lanka's eastern Valachchenai town, police said.
"Someone threw a hand grenade at some Moslem people near the office of the Assistant Superintendent of Police at about 1 a.m on Thursday night," police said.

One of the three killed was a soldier on home leave. Valachchenai, some 300 km (187 miles) from the capital Colombo, is a predominantly Moslem area in eastern Sri Lanka where government troops are fighting the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
The two communities have clashed in east Sri Lanka in the past and at least eight Moslems and three Tamils were killed in communal violence in the region in January.
Police said last month that in one instance the LTTE fired mortars at a Moslem village in eastern Batticaloa district, killing two people and wounding 11.
The LTTE are demanding a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east.
The government says the war, now in its 14th year, has killed more than 50,000 people. The LTTE says the number is higher.
